page: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled as a 500 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, this server demonstrates strong compute capabilities. Its stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranks in the top tier, while its multi-core performance falls within the top 25%. The AMD EPYC architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptographic acceleration. Software compilation via Clang and ray tracing tasks both achieve strong results in the top 25% tier. Memory performance is balanced, with Passmark memory scores in the top 25%, though raw memory bandwidth and database operations fall within the average range.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server is optimized for compute-heavy workloads rather than memory-intensive databases. It excels in tasks requiring high parallel processing power, such as software compilation, text generation using small language models, and cryptographic operations. However, workloads requiring massive memory footprints or high-capacity local storage may find the 64.0 GB RAM and 500 GB NVMe SSD limiting. It is best suited for CI/CD pipelines, web serving, and compute-bound application servers.
